revision_note: Rewritten after review. v1's five material errors are retracted and the report now separates proven facts, unexcluded hypotheses and required measurements. No exclusive conclusion is drawn.
author: DS-B
scope: Read-only independent investigation over /root/wksim-release-acceptance-fe3 sources and retained raw. No file in that workspace was modified; no native/ROS/SITL run, no build, no model load, no nested agent, no git. No analyzer extension and no instrumentation proposed for implementation.
question: Does manager/worker/Control lazy initialization, protocol decode, or log/async-writer preparation happen after the rate anchor?

verdict.statement: The call-site ordering in section proven is established. It does not prove that no first-time cost remains after the anchor, and it does not exclude log flush, I/O blocking, thread contention, decode CPU variation or host-periodic factors. No exclusive attribution is made.

retractions_from_v1.v1_claim: initialized.json plus ros_time_ns == 0 proves Control/task readiness and that all lazy initialization has finished
retractions_from_v1.correction: It only proves that the Task's named transport graph is ready. tools/pv_trajectory_task.py:40-52 request_graph_ready checks that setup_pub and command_pub each have exactly 2 subscribers on v2/setup and v2/command, that the node-name set is {wksim_joint_<stack>_control, recorder_name}, that namespaces are '/', and that the two endpoint GIDs are non-empty and distinct. It says nothing about Control's internal background activity.

retractions_from_v1.v1_claim: the tick-0 initial request fetched the 120-value initial state
retractions_from_v1.correction: That request never happened in these two fields. The runner sends a read-only snapshot (dict(version=1, epoch=..., snapshot=True)) which takes the worker's snapshot branch and answers state=None. The 120-value path is JointPhysics.initialize_states -> worker initial_request -> model.initial_state, and nothing in the flight path calls it.
retractions_from_v1.evidence: tools/run_joint_flight.py:901-903; Simulator/wksim_core/worker.py:88-92, 109-125, 151-152, 211-221, 238-245; Simulator/wksim_core/joint.py:69-93; only callers of initialize_states are Simulator/wksim_runtime/joint_runtime.py:705 and tools/probe_joint_terrain_feedback.py:716 (grep count in tools/run_joint_flight.py, tools/joint_pause_probe.py, tools/run-joint-flight.sh is 0 and the runner does not import joint_runtime); no *-truth.jsonl.initial.jsonl exists in either archive

retractions_from_v1.v1_claim: identical wire record counts and byte counts exclude log flush, I/O blocking and decode CPU variation
retractions_from_v1.correction: Record counts only show which record call sites were reached. wire.write targets a 65536-byte buffered file object and the wall field is read when the record dict is built, so identical counts say nothing about when bytes reach the kernel, about write blocking, about page-cache jitter, or about decode cost variation. The only per-stage wall/CPU evidence is the conditionally sampled diagnostic_step_cpu_timing, which is not a census.
retractions_from_v1.evidence: tools/run_joint_flight.py:801,812-816 (buffered writers and wall read at build time); Simulator/wksim_core/joint.py:215 (retention trigger wall_end-wall_start > 2 ms or tick%250==0)

retractions_from_v1.v1_claim: final_spin_other of about 900-960 us proves the release loop under-measures a segment
retractions_from_v1.correction: It is fully consistent with the code. The loop spins without health/sleep/record work only when remaining <= 1 ms, and the last sleep is only issued while remaining > 1 ms for min((remaining-1ms)/1e9, .002), so a roughly 1 ms spin is the designed expectation; sleep can also overshoot part of the margin. The probe's observed_elapsed closes the whole entry-to-terminal span and does not include the rate_group_start record write, which happens after actual_start_ns.
retractions_from_v1.evidence: Simulator/wksim_runtime/joint_rate.py:89-130 (branch structure, 1 ms threshold, 2 ms sleep cap, design comment); Simulator/wksim_runtime/joint_rate_probe.py:151-193 (closure identity and release_excess); measured sleep_max_overshoot means 93 us (first 250 groups) and 49.5 us (groups 5000-6000)

retractions_from_v1.v1_claim: spikes at different ticks in the two fields exclude a host-periodic event
retractions_from_v1.correction: The two fields ran at different times and this round established no common time mapping between their domains, so the observation cannot exclude a host-periodic factor. It is unexcluded.
retractions_from_v1.evidence: rate_anchor.anchor.wall_ns ztdsk269 1218406571925 vs vwen35gc 571735907115; no shared sampling marker in either field

retractions_from_v1.v1_claim: 250 intervals equals the first two seconds and matches the tool's split bit for bit
retractions_from_v1.correction: At 0.5x a 4-tick group spans 8 ms of ideal wall time, so 250 intervals is about 2 s of ideal wall time, but the block is this report's arbitrary measurement window, not the committed phase_partition. The real steady_after partition is early 246 (ztdsk269), 248 (vwen35gc), 249 (baseline). The two are different partitions and must not be called matching.

time_attribution_by_code.observed_elapsed: probe entry to terminal, where terminal is actual_start_ns; excludes the rate_group_start record write
time_attribution_by_code.final_spin_other: residual after subtracting the classified parts from observed_elapsed; equals spin wall time plus anything the classifier did not wrap
time_attribution_by_code.release_excess: terminal - earliest; independent of whether sleep occurred
time_attribution_by_code.group_work_ns: actual_start_ns to the paired rate_group_end.actual_end_ns, so the rate_group_start record write and the return to the caller fall at the start of the next group's work_ns

wire_event_sequence_within_one_field.note: reliable as a sequence; it establishes no mapping between the wire wall domain and the rate absolute-ns domain

unexcluded.why: wire record counts and byte counts show only which call sites were reached and how many bytes were serialized; writes go to a 65536-byte buffered file object and the wall field is read when the record is built, so kernel write timing, blocking and page-cache jitter are unmeasured
no measurement isolates competition between the manager thread and the process's other threads or between the manager and its children

equal byte counts do not imply equal decode cost; the only per-stage evidence is the conditionally sampled diagnostic_step_cpu_timing, which retained only 22 records in ticks 40..1200 for ztdsk269 and is not a census
the two fields ran at different times and no common time mapping was established, so different spike ticks cannot exclude a host-periodic factor

physics_health (tools/run_joint_flight.py:570-583) is passed into begin_group at tools/run_joint_flight.py:919 and runs roughly every 2 ms there; the probe records its call count and cumulative wall time inside begin_group but no per-part cost

the call-site ordering proves these sites ran before the anchor; it does not prove that no first execution remains inside Control, in DDS thread wakeups, or in a first subscription callback inside pause_probe.pump()
